title: Portal Jump
pageTitle: Ordered Pairs in All Four Quadrants
covers: how the signs of an ordered pair tell which of the four quadrants a point is in, and how to plot and move between points in all four quadrants
cert: naming quadrants from the signs of ordered pairs and plotting points in all four quadrants

intro.caption: Lesson 7-8 — ordered pairs in all four quadrants. Floor −8 is the Portal Hall. Two glowing lines cross in the middle of the floor, and every portal sits at an ordered pair. Pick the right portal and you jump ahead. Pick the wrong one and... well.

balloons.t: Those lines are the x-axis and the y-axis. They split the floor into four quadrants.
The exit portal is at (3, −4)! Everybody wait for the plan. EVERYBODY. Kwame?
(3, −4)! Three steps left, four steps up. GO!
You went to (−3, 4). Both signs flipped. Wrong quadrant, right into the slime.

pages.caption: The signs tell the direction. Positive x goes right, negative x goes left. Positive y goes up, negative y goes down. (3, −4) is right 3, down 4.

balloons.t: Quadrants go counterclockwise: I top right, II top left, III bottom left, IV bottom right.

pages.ch: Chapter 2 · Path A or Path B?

balloons.t: Two paths. Path A has a portal at (−3, −5). Path B has the slime. I pick A!
Plot it first! Start at the origin, (0, 0). x moves you across, y moves you up or down.
The floor stones only let you walk straight: across or up and down. Each hop changes x or y.
I'm walking behind you this time. Way behind.
The REAL exit portal! Six left, one down. My map says it's in Quadrant II. Only ten gold!
Six left and one down? Let's check the signs before we pay anything.
I kept my eyes closed the WHOLE time.
Right quadrant, right portal, right into the treasure! Kwame, you can open your eyes.

win.caption: Quadrant I is (+, +), II is (−, +), III is (−, −) and IV is (+, −). A point with a 0 coordinate sits on an axis, not in a quadrant. Read the signs before you jump.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Name the Quadrant
gates.badge: Quadrant Reader — Signs of Ordered Pairs
gates.prompt: Each portal stone sits at an ordered pair. Use the signs to name its quadrant.
hints: Conceptual: the sign of x tells left (−) or right (+). The sign of y tells down (−) or up (+). Together they pick one quadrant.
Procedural: write the signs as (±, ±). Then match: I (+, +), II (−, +), III (−, −), IV (+, −).

steps: x = −2 is negative, so it is left of the y-axis. y = −6 is negative, so it is below the x-axis.
Signs (−, −): left and down. That is Quadrant III.

items.q: A portal stone glows at (−4, 3). Which quadrant is it in?

options.fb: Quadrant I needs both signs positive. x = −4 is negative, so the stone is on the left.
Quadrant III needs both signs negative. y = 3 is positive, so the stone is above the x-axis.
Quadrant IV is (+, −): right and down. This stone is left and up.

items.q: Another stone is at (2, −5). Which quadrant?

options.fb: Quadrant III is (−, −). x = 2 is positive, so the stone is on the right.
Quadrant II is (−, +): left and up. This stone is right and down.
Quadrant I is (+, +). y = −5 is negative, so the stone is below the x-axis.
(1, −6) is right and down, (+, −). That is Quadrant IV.
(−1, 6) is left and up, (−, +). That is Quadrant II.
(6, 1) is right and up, (+, +). That is Quadrant I.

gates.pass: Three stones, three quadrants, zero slime. Sol adds a sign chart to the map.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Plot the Portal
gates.prompt: Path A's portal is at (−3, −5). Plot it, then mark the two safe stones.
hints: Conceptual: x always comes first. A negative x means go LEFT from the origin; a negative y means go DOWN.
Procedural: start at (0, 0). Move across by x. Then move up or down by y. Place the dot.

steps: Practice point: (−1, 4). Start at the origin, (0, 0).
x = −1 is negative, so move 1 unit LEFT.
y = 4 is positive, so move 4 units UP. The point is in Quadrant II.
worked.q: How do you move from the origin to plot (5, −2)?

items.q: Tap the Path A portal at (−3, −5).

fb.msg: That's (3, −5). The x is −3, so go LEFT 3, not right.
That's (−3, 5). The y is −5, so go DOWN 5, not up.
That's (−5, −3): x and y are swapped. Move across by x = −3 first, then down by 5.
That's (3, 5). Both signs flipped, just like Kwame. Both numbers are negative: left 3, down 5.

items.fbDefault: Start at (0, 0). Go left 3, then down 5.

fb.msg: That's (−4, 0): x and y are swapped. For (0, −4), x = 0 means do not move across. Just go down 4.
That's (2, −6): x and y are swapped. For (−6, 2), go left 6 first, then up 2.
That's (6, 2). The x is −6, so go LEFT 6.
That's (0, 4). The y is −4, so go DOWN 4.

items.fbDefault: You need two points. (0, −4) sits on the y-axis. (−6, 2) is left 6, up 2.

gates.pass: Path A's portal is plotted in Quadrant III, and (0, −4) sits right on the y-axis, in no quadrant at all. The party hops through, dry.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Navigate the Floor
gates.prompt: The floor stones only move you straight across or straight up and down. Follow the hops.
hints: Conceptual: moving right or left changes only x. Moving up or down changes only y.
Procedural: right adds to x, left subtracts from x. Up adds to y, down subtracts from y.

steps: Practice: start at (1, −2). Move 3 left and 4 up.
You land at (−2, 2), which is (−, +), Quadrant II.
worked.q: Start at (0, 0). Move 4 left and 1 down. Where do you land?

items.q: Start at (−2, 3). Hop 5 right, then 6 down. Tap where you land.

fb.msg: You moved to y = −6. Moving 6 DOWN from y = 3 gives 3 − 6 = −3.
You moved right but not down. Now hop 6 down: 3 − 6 = −3.
That's (−3, 3). Moving right from x = −2 means adding: −2 + 5 = 3.
Right y, wrong sign on x. Moving 5 right from −2 crosses the y-axis: −2 + 5 = 3.

items.fbDefault: x: −2 + 5. y: 3 − 6. Then tap that point.

items.q: Anya walks straight up from (−4, −2) to (−4, 5). Which quadrants does she walk through?

options.fb: x stays −4 the whole walk, so she never leaves the left side. Quadrant I is on the right.
Right quadrants, wrong order. She walks UP: she starts below the x-axis in III and ends above it in II.
IV and I are on the right side, where x is positive. Her x is −4, so she is on the left.

gates.pass: Hop, hop, land at (3, −3). Anya crosses from III into II without a single slip.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Grimble's Portal Map
gates.prompt: Grimble says the exit portal is 6 units left and 1 unit down from the origin, and that it's in Quadrant II. Check everything.
hints: Conceptual: left means a negative x and down means a negative y. The signs together decide the quadrant.
Procedural: write the ordered pair first, (x, y). Then write its signs and match them to a quadrant.

steps: Practice: a point 2 units right and 6 units up.
Right 2 means x = 2. Up 6 means y = 6. The point is (2, 6).
Signs (+, +), so it is in Quadrant I.
worked.q: A point is 5 left and 3 down from the origin. What are its coordinates and quadrant?

items.q: Tap the exit portal: 6 units left and 1 unit down from the origin.

fb.msg: That's (6, −1), 6 units RIGHT. Left means a negative x.
That's (−6, 1), 1 unit UP. Down means a negative y.
That's (−1, −6): x and y are swapped. The 6 units left is the x.
That's (6, 1). Both signs flipped. Left and down are both negative.

items.fbDefault: Start at (0, 0). Go 6 left, then 1 down.

items.q: Grimble's map says the portal at (−6, −1) is in Quadrant II. What's the truth?

options.t: Grimble is right: it's on the left, so Quadrant II.
options.fb: Left only tells you about x. y = −1 is below the x-axis, and Quadrant II is above it.

options.t: Quadrant IV, because y is negative.
options.fb: Quadrant IV needs a positive x. Here x = −6 is negative.

options.t: Quadrant III, because x and y are both negative.
No quadrant, because it is close to an axis.
options.fb: Only a point with a 0 coordinate sits on an axis. (−6, −1) has no zero, so it is in a quadrant.

items.q: Last lock: what signs does every point in Quadrant IV have?

options.fb: (−, +) is left and up. That is Quadrant II.
(−, −) is left and down. That is Quadrant III.
(+, +) is right and up. That is Quadrant I.

gates.pass: The portal is at (−6, −1), Quadrant III, not II. Grimble pockets his map and mumbles something about "a printing error."

journal.heading: Lesson 7-8 — what the portal jump taught us
rows: (x, y): x moves across, y moves up or down. Negative x goes left. Negative y goes down.
I (+, +) top right. II (−, +) top left. III (−, −) bottom left. IV (+, −) bottom right.
(0, −4) has a 0, so it sits on the y-axis, in no quadrant.
He read (3, −4) as left 3, up 4 and landed at (−3, 4). Flip one sign and you are in a different quadrant.
journal.quote: "Signs first, then jump. Or enjoy the slime." — Pip

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 7-8 (Ordered Pairs in All Four Quadrants) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: plotting ordered pairs in all four quadrants, naming a quadrant from the signs of the coordinates, points on an axis, and moving across and up or down between points.
standards: Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants of the coordinate plane
